title: A made-up key that CC8 can't catch
story: As 4.2-cc8-made-up-key, but the teen removes three words of A3 by hand in its content reveal. A turn whose reveal removed a span gets only the es rule, so CC8 can compare A3 with nothing, and it passes. This is the limit DESIGN 7.3 and ledger-v1.md 10.8 state.
edits: The transcript's user entry for each prompt, read by the log reader 0.7 to 4.5 s after the hook (via log, same turn_key and lengths), as a real Claude Code client records it.
A3's f is computed under a made-up key. In A3's reveal, words 3, 6 and 9 (`sidebar`, `an`, `on`) are removed as type teen, so CC8 can compare A3 with nothing.

CC5.basis: one device, whose scorer credits each slot to at most one project (SM 3.1)

CC6.basis: Stated, not recomputed: the live buckets are pkg/score over this device's events.jsonl, which the reveal holds in full, so the server's re-score is the same computation and every minute reproduces.

CC10.reason: no editor act in the submission

known_limit: DESIGN 7.3 and ledger-v1.md 10.8: a client that keys a turn's features under a key of its own is caught only through another revealed turn with the same normalized text, and a span removed by hand hides the turn from every CC8 rule but es. Issue #15's decision accepted this.
notes: A reviewer reading A3's kept text, `make the ... collapse into ... icon rail ... small screens`, can still see the re-roll. CC8, the automatic check, can't.
